title: Air-Fryer Fish Fingers
subtitle: Homemade fish fingers from the air fryer
excerpt: Thick cod goujons coated in seasoned breadcrumbs and cooked in the air fryer until crisp on the outside and flaky inside. Better than any box and ready in 20 minutes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Fish fingers are one of the great British convenience foods: introduced by Birds Eye in 1955, they quickly became a staple of British family cooking. Homemade fish fingers use a proper fillet of white fish instead of minced fish pieces, and the coating is seasoned breadcrumbs rather than a thick batter. The air fryer crisps the coating without deep-frying and avoids the mess of pan-frying.

content.text: The standard three-stage coating is flour, egg, breadcrumbs: flour dries the surface so the egg sticks; egg acts as glue for the breadcrumbs. Press the breadcrumbs firmly onto each piece. Spray or brush lightly with oil just before cooking: the oil helps the breadcrumbs colour evenly.

items.preparation: cut into finger-sized pieces, about 8 cm long

content.text: Set up three shallow bowls: one with the flour seasoned with salt and pepper, one with the beaten egg, one with the breadcrumbs mixed with smoked paprika.
Pat the cod pieces dry. Coat each piece in flour, then beaten egg, then breadcrumbs, pressing firmly to adhere. Place on a plate.
Preheat the air fryer to 200 C for 3 minutes. Brush or spray the coated fish fingers lightly with oil. Place in the air fryer basket in a single layer.
Cook at 200 C for 10 to 12 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and crisp. The fish inside should be opaque and flake easily. Serve with chips and peas.
